 2026 Australian MotoGP race at Phillip Island today: Start times and how to watch
 Information below on how to watch this weekend’s 2026 Australian MotoGP round at the Phillip Island, including timings and schedule.
 Peter McLaren Updated: 24 Oct 2026 Share This weekend's schedule for the Australian MotoGP at Phillip Island. © Gold and Goose Prefer Crash.Net on Google See our stories more often Add Update: Sunday's track action has been delayed due to bad weather . 
 This is how to watch the 2026 Australian MotoGP at Phillip Island, round 18 of the world championship, which takes place from 23-25 October.
 We’ve also listed the start times for all this weekend’s MotoGP sessions below, in both local time and UK time.
 MotoGP machines will take to the legendary Phillip Island circuit for the last time, at least for the foreseeable future, during this weekend’s Australian Grand Prix.
 Phillip Island held its first Australian Grand Prix in 1989 and, the 2020 and 2021 Covid cancellations aside, has hosted the event continuously since 1997. However, the event will move to the new Adelaide ‘street circuit’ from 2027.
 Article continues below ADVERTISEMENT Article continues below ADVERTISEMENT Phillip Island circuit, Australia. © Gold and Goose The final Phillip Island round began with just two points separating Jorge Martin and Marc Marquez at the top of the standings.
 A dramatic Saturday saw Marquez snatch pole in the wet qualifying, before Martin went on the attack in the dry Sprint - only to crash and sustain arm injuries while battling Marquez for the lead, ruling him out of the grand prix.
 That gives Marquez a golden opportunity to extend his ten-point advantage on Sunday, when the worst weather of the weekend is expected.
 Marquez and Martin both missed Phillip Island last season due to injuries, when Marco Bezzecchi and Raul Fernandez completed an Aprilia double of Sprint and Grand Prix victories.
 Article continues below ADVERTISEMENT Article continues below ADVERTISEMENT However, Marquez is a four-time Phillip Island MotoGP winner, including on his only previous Ducati appearance with Gresini in 2024, and will fancy his chances at a track where MotoGP’s best traditionally rise to the top.
 The only other former Phillip Island winners on the grid are Fernandez, Johann Zarco and Alex Rins, with just one victory apiece. Home hero Jack Miller will also make his final Australian MotoGP appearance before moving to WorldSBK next season.
 As always, the weather will play a major role, with sunshine for Friday practice replaced by Saturday's showers. Even heavier rain is forecast for Sunday.
 Fabio Quartararo dodges a wallaby at Phillip Island. © Gold and Goose When is the 2026 Australian MotoGP? 
 The Australian MotoGP round at Phillip Island runs from 23-25 October.
 Article continues below ADVERTISEMENT Article continues below ADVERTISEMENT Two free practice sessions will be held on Friday, 23 October. Final practice, qualifying and the Sprint race are on Saturday, 24 October. Warm-up and the grand prix are on Sunday, 25 October.
 What are the start times for the 2026 Australian MotoGP? 
 Friday 23 October: 
10:45am (local)/00:45am (UK) - MotoGP FP1
3:00pm (local)/5:00am (UK) - MotoGP Practice
 Saturday 24 October: 
10:10am (local)/00:10am (UK) - MotoGP FP2
10:50am (local)/00:50am (UK) - MotoGP Qualifying
3:00pm (local)/5:00am (UK) - MotoGP Sprint
 Sunday 25 October: 
 8:40am (local)/23:40am (Sat, UK) - MotoGP Warm-up
 Article continues below ADVERTISEMENT Article continues below ADVERTISEMENT 2:00pm (local)/3:00am (UK) - MotoGP Race
 Marco Bezzecchi leads Raul Fernandez, 2025 Australian MotoGP Sprint at Phillip Island. © Gold and Goose How to watch the 2026 Australian MotoGP? 
 The 2026 Australia MotoGP is available to live stream for free on Austrian service ServusTV .While the service is restricted to geo-restricted to Austria, UK viewers can get access to the free service via a VPN. These tools can hide your real IP address (digital location) and connect you to a secure server in Austria, allowing you to bypass geo-restrictions to access ServusTV from anywhere in the world. 
 Unblock free streaming services like ServusTV by doing the following: 
 1. Sign up to NordVPN .

 MotoGP's official Video Pass streaming service will also broadcast all of the sessions live.
 MotoGP Video Pass costs €148.99 for the whole season including Timing Pass, or €139.99 for the whole season without live data.

 Alternatively, for UK-based fans, TNT Sports is showing every session of the Australian MotoGP.
 A subscription to TNT Sports through HBO Max starts from £27.99 per month, depending on your plans.
